title: Parallelize reranker batching and implement per-candidate token caps to reduce p95 latency
creator: Sofia Martinez
description:
Background: The reranking endpoint scores variable-length candidate lists (up to N candidates per request) using a cross-encoder model. Recent customer reports and synthetic load tests show large p95 tail latency spikes when requests include many long candidates. Investigation indicates two main contributors: (1) naive batching that groups requests only by arrival time leading to batches with extreme token-count variance, and (2) single-threaded scoring per request inside a batch which creates head-of-line blocking for long sequences.

Goal: Reduce p95 latency and tail variability for the reranking endpoint without degrading score quality or significantly increasing cost. Primary levers: parallelize scoring within batches (slice by token-cost), enforce adaptive per-candidate token caps with truncation policies, and introduce timeouts/early-exit heuristics for very long candidate lists.

Scope: Implementation touches rerank service batching layer, runtime inference shard logic, API input validation, and rollout/metrics dashboards. Must include benchmarks, A/B canary rollout, and a rollback plan.
acceptance_criteria: p95 serving latency for mixed workloads reduced by >=35% compared to baseline (measured over a 72h synthetic + customer trace window)
No measurable drop in reranking quality (NDCG@10 change within ±0.5% on held-out eval set)
Per-request CPU and GPU utilization remains within 110% of baseline for steady-state traffic
New batching logic has unit and integration tests covering batch slicing, token-cap policies, and timeout behavior
Canary rollout for 5% of production traffic completes with automated rollback on error spikes or quality regressions
tasks: Design batch-slicing algorithm: group candidates by token-cost into sub-batches and prioritize low-token sub-batches for faster completion
Add parallel scoring worker pool inside inference process to process sub-batches concurrently
Implement per-candidate token cap and truncation policy configurable by model profile (default 1024 tokens for rerank cross-encoder)
Expose new timeout and early-exit controls at API layer (request-level timeout and per-candidate soft timeout)
Instrument metrics: p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens-per-request distribution, batch composition stats, quality metrics (NDCG), and cost per request
Benchmarks: run mixed workload tests (short/medium/long candidates) and collect 72h results
Create canary rollout dashboard and automated alert rules (latency 2x baseline or quality drop >1%)
Docs: update API spec with token limits and new error codes; add migration notes for SDK clients
comments: 2026-02-21 - Priya Anand (PM): Prioritizing this P0 due to customer escalations from two enterprise accounts. Please include a conservative default token cap and a knob to disable truncation for opt-in customers.

2026-02-26 - Daniel Wu: Initial prototype of batch-slicing complete. Tested locally with synthetic microbenchmarks; p95 improved ~28% but single long-request still blocks GPU for up to 3s. Planning parallel worker pool next.

2026-03-02 - Rachel Kim (ML Infra): Reviewed prototype. Feedback: ensure we maintain deterministic scoring order for audit logs and tie-breakers; implement deterministic seed for any parallelism-related nondeterminism.

2026-03-05 - Liam O'Connor (SRE): Noted potential risk for increased GPU memory fragmentation with concurrent sub-batch kernels. Suggest soft cap on concurrent workers per GPU and fallback serial path.

2026-03-09 - Daniel Wu: Integrated per-candidate truncation and added soft timeouts. Ran 24h mixed traffic bench against staging: p95 improved 42%, NDCG delta +0.02% (within tolerance). Opening PR for review: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rerank-service/pull/412
2026-03-11 - Sofia Martinez: Design review: approve performance vs quality trade-offs. Request to publish config defaults and recommended migration steps in the runbook before canary.
2026-03-12 - Daniel Wu: Canary scheduled for 2026-03-15 targeting 5% traffic. Dashboard and alerts configured: https://console.redwood.ai/dashboards/rerank-batching-canary
notes: Trade-offs considered: (1) aggressive truncation reduces latency but can hurt relevance for long candidates — mitigated by conservative default and opt-in disable; (2) deeper parallelism improves tail but increases GPU kernel churn and memory pressure — mitigated by concurrency cap and adaptive scheduler.
Rollout plan: dev unit tests -> staging integration -> 5% canary with automated quality checks -> 25% -> 100%. Rollback triggers: p95 latency > 2x baseline or NDCG@10 drop >1.0% on eval probes.
Follow-ups: explore candidate pre-filtering using cheap embedding dot-product to reduce number of scored candidates for heavy requests (ENG-8874 backlog).
